title: Body sections by kind, and the form a body takes
description:
The two headings each kind names, in order, and the rules the body itself obeys. A body carries exactly these two and no third heading; a section with no content carries the literal line `None.`

**Nothing verifies this table today.** The analysis places the headings and the enrichment fills them, and `check_field_ownership.py` compares the headings against the seal — that is, against what the analysis itself wrote. A kind given the wrong two headings is never compared to this table, and the body-length ceiling the base declares is read by no shipped script at all.

x-form.one_sentence_per_line: A body places one sentence per line.
x-form.rfc2119: A normative statement uses exactly one RFC 2119 keyword, in uppercase, and no pronoun.
x-form.no_third_heading: A third heading is one the contract refuses.
x-form.empty_section: A section with no content carries the literal line `None.`
x-form.no_rationale: A body carries no rationale, history, alternatives, or motivating narrative, and is never the only place a fact a machine reads appears.
x-form.no_alias: A synonym is declared in `aliases` and appears in no body.
x-form.ceiling: The body-length ceiling comes from `limits.body_lines` in the base's own system declaration. The framework supplies no value: where the declaration is absent, the check reports itself unenforceable rather than assuming one.

x-open: No shipped script reads `limits.body_lines`, so the ceiling is declared, validated in shape, and enforced by nothing.
No shipped script compares a body's headings against this table.
